clauses.reason: The lead clause says the President does "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and is hereby approved", with the approval stated to be "subject to the following condition". That is a section 3(a) approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry with no stated period. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Condition (1) provides that "a Photographic Manufacturing Industry Committee be created to cooperate with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry", and that the committee "which committee shall consist of seven representatives of the Photographic Manufacturing Industry elected by a fair method of selection". It is imposed as a condition of the approval of the code (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3, section 3(a)), so it qualifies the approval and has no operative force apart from it. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. No held record shows the committee formed or the Administrator's three non-voting appointments made, so the claim does not date any performance of the condition; it records only that the condition, as a term of the approval, ended with the approval on June 14, 1935, and treats any committee actually formed as an accrued consequence.

research_rationale:
Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6257 is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362077), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2024-12-04T12:59:10Z whose heading names Executive Order 6257, whose date (August 19, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1933 Aug 19 p.536: Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufac turing Industry approved. I NRA Codes 209. [ 521 ]) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The machine inventory (a lead approval clause and condition (1)) matches the text, so no inventory correction was needed.

Searched the held order texts (jobs/*/output/texts, through the Cruden lookup and a follow-up regex search on the code's name), the census register and the WPA 1944 list for later orders citing EO 6257 by number or naming its code: no held order text cites this order by number and no other held text names the code, so nothing earlier than the repeal is established. Section 3(a) of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) lets the President impose conditions \"as a condition of his approval of any such code\", and the order states this requirement as a condition of its approval, citing only Title I and the general words \"and otherwise\"; it names no other statute, so it is not a separate appointment or delegation under another authority. No held record shows the committee created, its members elected or appointed, or the committee dissolved, so no performance date or earlier end is claimed. savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. A committee actually created under condition (1) and any members chosen or appointed for it are accrued consequences of the order; this claim records no continuing command to create or maintain the committee.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
